title: Keep a class nonnegative
prompt: A Quantity begins at zero. add(amount) accepts only positive amounts and keeps the total at most 1000. take(amount) accepts only positive amounts no larger than the current total. Rejected calls return false without changing the total.
signature: class Quantity: bool add(int); bool take(int); int value() const
starter:
#include <iostream>

class Quantity{int value_{};public:bool add(int amount){if(amount<=0||amount>1000-value_)return false;value_+=amount;return true;}bool take(int amount){value_-=amount;return true;}int value()const{return value_;}};
solution:
#include <iostream>

class Quantity{int value_{};public:bool add(int amount){if(amount<=0||amount>1000-value_)return false;value_+=amount;return true;}bool take(int amount){if(amount<=0||amount>value_)return false;value_-=amount;return true;}int value()const{return value_;}};

tests.label: Add and take
tests.hint: Take subtracts from the stored total.

tests.label: Cannot overdraw
tests.hint: Reject if taking more than is present.

tests.label: Reject zero take
tests.hint: The contract requires a positive amount.

tests.label: Reject negative take
tests.hint: Do not let subtraction of a negative increase the total.

hints: Return false on rejection without changing any stored state.
explanation: The class keeps its balance private, so callers cannot bypass add/take. Each method must preserve 0 <= value <= 1000.
